models.name: Model G
models.summary: Introduced in 1936 in "monofilm" and "multifilm" models; the multifilm included a tool-free parts kit of reel spindles, sprockets, gate and guide-rollers to adapt the projector to various film gauges.
Projected 8mm film at fixed speeds of 18 and 5 frames per second forward, and 18 fps in reverse.

models.name: M-8
models.summary: Designed to run off a mains power supply of 110–125 Volts.

models.name: SM 8
models.summary: Magnetic sound projection and recording, with a built-in 2W / 15 Ohm speaker.

models.name: S-221
models.summary: Plays back silent or sound film with optical or magnetic tracks, and records sound onto 16mm magnetic-striped film.

models.name: SM 80 Programmatic
models.summary: The top of Bolex's Super 8 sound range at the end of the 1970s, and a different machine from the SP 80 despite the name. It records on both sound tracks rather than one, takes 800ft reels rather than 600, and carries a Bolex Hi-Fi f/1.2 12.5 to 25mm zoom and a 100W halogen lamp with a dichroic reflector. A track selector gives either track or both, with fading, sound-on-sound, an automatic level limiter, manual override and an LED meter; a sync socket also drives an outside tape recorder, so it works single or double system. 18 and 24 frames a second, with a counter. Built in Austria by Eumig. Bolex (U.S.A.) listed it at $780.00 in April 1979, the dearest projector on the page.

sources.title: Bolex Super 8 Cameras and Projectors, price list no. S1, 1 April 1979
sources.note: Bolex (U.S.A.) Inc.'s own list: "Bolex SM-80 Programmatic", product 93480, $780.00 suggested retail. Read off the rendered page, which matters here: the scan's text layer runs the neighbouring rows' model numbers into their lens specifications and invents models that do not exist. The list hyphenates the name; this entry does not, to match the SM 8 and SP 80 beside it.

sources.title: Super8Data, Bolex SM 80 Programmatic
sources.note: A collector database, so secondary. Everything above except the price comes from it, and it is also what settles the machine's identity: it dates the SM 80 Programmatic to 1977 with a 240m reel, recording on both tracks and a f/1.2 12.5 to 25mm lens, against the SP 80's 1973 to 1974 run, 180m reel and single track. The two are not the same projector under two names, which is the easy mistake to make from the price list alone.

models.name: SP 8
models.summary: A Super 8 magnetic sound projector that records as well as plays back, sold from 1972 with a f/1.3 15 to 30mm zoom, a 100W 12V lamp, automatic threading, forward and reverse running, 18 and 24 frames a second and 600ft reels. Sound goes on the main track, with fading and sound-on-sound, and the level can be set by hand or left to an automatic limiter. Built in Austria by Eumig, who had bought Bolex in 1969, on the same chassis as Eumig's own Mark S. Paillard's February 1972 dealer list prices it at $299.50, between the 18-5L Super at $199.50 and the SM8 Sound at $449.50. A SP 8 Special was also sold, and the later SP 80 is built on it.

sources.title: Bolex Super 8mm Confidential Price List, 23 February 1972
sources.note: The primary source, and the reason this entry exists. Paillard's own dealer list: "SP8 SOUND, product 2480, w/f/1.3 15-30mm Zoom Lens", $299.50 suggested retail. Read off the rendered page. Scanned by Pacific Rim Camera.

sources.title: Super8Data, Bolex SP 8
sources.note: A collector database, so secondary, but it dates the machine to 1972 and gives the same f/1.3 15 to 30mm lens the price list does, which is the two sources agreeing without having seen each other. Everything above beyond the price and the lens comes from here: the lamp, the reel size, the speeds, the sound arrangement and the Eumig Mark S chassis. The specifications it gives beyond that, down to the amplifier's transistor count, have not been repeated here because none of them has been checked against a Bolex document.

models.name: SP 80
models.summary: A Super 8 and Single-8 projector with magnetic sound it can both record and play back, with automatic threading, forward and reverse running, 18 and 24 frames a second and 600ft reels. From after Eumig acquired Bolex in 1969, and built on Eumig's own mechanism rather than a Sainte-Croix design. A variant was sold as the SP 80 Special.

sources.title: Dealer and collector listings, read November 2026
sources.note: Everything above comes from people selling or restoring the machine, not from Paillard or Eumig. They agree on the format, the sound, the speeds and the reel size, and date it to 1973 to 1975. They disagree on which Eumig chassis underlies it, the 700 or the 800 series, so this entry does not say. No manufacturer document has been read, and one is wanted.
